terminal_name: Naip and Bagaja liquefied-gas plants (Lebap region)
issue: Turkmen state press (newscentralasia, oilgas.gov.tm, business.com.tm) repeatedly calls the Naip (Darganata district) and Bagaja/Bagadja (Charjev/Karakum) plants 'LNG' production complexes, operated by Turkmengaz's Lebap Liquefied Gas Production directorate. Investigation shows these are LPG (liquefied petroleum gas / propane-butane) facilities co-producing gas condensate, not methane LNG terminals: 'LNG' is a mistranslation of Turkmen 'suwuklandyrylan gaz' (= liquefied gas/LPG). Decisive primary signal: Trend.Az (2026) reports Lebap-region LPG output >30,000 t in 4M2026, explicitly 'liquefied petroleum gas (LPG)'; Bagaja produced 9,713 t 'liquefied gas' + 23,850 t gas condensate in 2021; Naip plant commissioned 1998 by Italy's Technofrigo, later Naip+Bagaja built by Canada's Thermo Design Engineering. These are gas-processing/LPG plants, OUT OF SCOPE for the GEM LNG terminals tracker. NOT staged as new terminals.
suggested_action: No action. Documented so future discovery sweeps do not re-investigate Naip/Bagaja as LNG terminals; they are LPG/gas-processing facilities. The only genuine Turkmenistan LNG facility remains Kiyanly LNG Terminal (T100000130827), already in GEM.

issue: Trade-press analysis (naturalgasworld, Hudson, energynews.pro) discusses LNG as a theoretical westward export option for Turkmenistan given landlocked/Caspian constraints, but there is NO identified sponsor, no concrete project, no FID/MOU for any new Caspian liquefaction/transshipment terminal. The Trans-Caspian Gas Pipeline is a pipeline (not an LNG terminal). Below the 'sufficient information to add' bar; no monitor record warranted (pre-sponsor, no concrete step).
suggested_action: No action; revisit only if a named sponsor announces a concrete Caspian LNG export/transshipment terminal.
